title: EGY-02 · Nominal phrase, demonstration, miš, numbers and prices

blocks.text: EGY-02 · Nominal phrase, demonstration, miš, numbers and prices
Lesson overview

With the Egyptian of EGY-01 You can introduce yourself. Now you learn to say what they are and how things are: ... this is dear, ... that's not new, ... ..there's Turkish coffee? These are the phrases of the store, the market and the house. Study Egyptian demos, which go after the name, denial miš, the numbers with their abbreviated forms and the way to ask and bargain a price. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-03, B1-04 and B1-05.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 101–106), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, tutor recordings on the phone
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. build nominal phrases in Egyptian (il-maḥall from kbīr, ana miš fāhim);
2. use demonstration from, to, dōl in the right position;
3. deny with miš, ma-fīš and ma-ʿandīš;
4. count from 1 a 1000 and use numbers with names (talat kutub, ʿišrīn ginēh);
5. ask for a price, comment on it, bargain and pay.
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

2. The nominal sentence
As in fuṣḥā, at present the verb is not there.

fīh There is, there are, it is unchangeable: fīh ʿēš There's bread. fīh nās kitīr There's a lot of people. In one question, the intonation is enough: fīh ʾahwa? Is there coffee? The adjective agrees as in fuṣḥā: il-maḥall kbīr, il-ʾōḍa kbīra. In the plural of things the adjective often goes to the singular female, as in fuṣḥā (il-ḥagāt of ġalya These things are dear, but the plural is also heard in the speech (ġalyīn).
3. Demonstration
plural dōl dukham
The location. It is the main difference with the fuṣḥā: The demo goes after the name with the article.

Two functions. il-kitāb from • this book (syntagma) · from kitāb This is a book, "Prase." As in fuṣḥā, the article makes a difference. To indicate things in the speech is also used a lot by a gesture: ēh From? What is this? mīn of? Who's this? Time. il-yōm from ...today (letters This day is the day, il-usbūʿ from this week onwards, is-healthy of ... this year.
4. Denial: miš, ma-fīš, ma-ʿandīš

rows: from miš ġāli · ana miš fāhim

blocks.text: present with b- miš or but...-š miš baštaġal / ma-baštaġalš non-work

ma-fīš and ma-ʿandīš. Denial but...-š surrounds the word: but + fīh + š → ma-fīš; but + ʿandi + š → but- ʿandīš. The forms of ʿand-: ma-ʿandīš I don't have any. ma-ʿandakš "non-hay' (m.), ma-ʿandikīš "N'-n'-n'-n'-n' (f.), ma-ʿandūš "Handleless', ma-ʿandahāš "No ha" (she), ma-ʿandināš We don't have any. ma-fīš muškila "No problem" is one of the most frequent phrases in Egyptian.
5. Numbers

The compounds are said as in fuṣḥā, first the unit: wāḥid w-ʿišrīn «21», sabʿa w-talatīn «37• • • • • • • • • • • w-ḫamsa w- arbiʿīn «145». Hundreds (recognize): tultumiyya300», rubʿumiyya «400», ḫumsumiyya «500• • • • •600», subʿumiyya «700• • • •800», tusʿumiyya «900»; alfēn «2000• , talat t-alāf «3000». The prices. nuṣṣ "Mezzo" is the name of the vessel. rubʿ 4th of a kind used in the manufacture of goods of heading 8511: ḫamsa w-nuṣṣ 5 and a half, ginēh w-rubʿ 1 pound and 25 cents. The Egyptian pound is the ginēh ; the plate, a penny of sterling, is the ʾirš (pl. ʾurūš), now used almost only in the ways of saying.

blocks.text: Short forms (3–10) before the name: talat, arbaʿ, ḫamas, sitt, sabaʿ, taman, tisaʿ, ʿašar. In front of some plurals that begin by vowel inserts a t: talat t-iyyām 3 days ḫamas t-alāf Five thousand. With the units of measurement and coins the talk is more free: you also hear itnēn kīlu and talāta yūro. It's normal in prices.

8. To the shop and market

rows: He's not here. · We don't have any.

blocks.text: Contracting is normal in markets and small shops in Cairo, not in supermarkets, pharmacies and shops with exposed prices. It is done with a smile: too low a price, bad said, is rude.
9. Pronunciation

The numbers. Attention to short vowels that fall: arbaʿtāšar, ḫamastāšar, sabaʿtāšar. ʿišrīn is pronounced with the ʿ well-heard at first. talatīn and tamanīn : t ṯ. The ʾ from ⁧ق⁩ in prices. ʾirš, ʾifl, daʾāyiʾ Minutes (fuṣḥā ⁧دَقَائِق⁩ ): pronounce the glottal stop, not a k. Shadowing. The tutor reads the dialog 1 at normal speed; You repeat Luke's lines and then those of ʿAmm Fatḥi, imitating the tone as a merchant.

13. Oral production
1. What is this? (session). The tutor indicates ten objects in the room or in photos: answer with / from / dōl + name + adjective (from kitāb ʾadīmof ʿarabiyya gdīda).
2. To the market (role game). The tutor is a seller at the market: buy three things, ask for prices, contract At least once, pay.
3. What is there and what is not there. Describe your kitchen or office in one minute: fīh…, ma-fīš…, ʿandi…, ma-ʿandīš….
